newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle lands in Florida.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle lands in Florida.

text.p: The U.S. space shuttle Alantis landed in Florida on Saturday, bringing home U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger from a troubled mission to Russia's Mir space station.
The winged spaceship swooped out of a partly cloudy sky and touched down on the three-mile (5 km) runway at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre at 9:27 a.m. EDT (1327 GMT).

Linenger, the fourth NASA astronaut to live and work aboard Mir, was experiencing the pull of gravity for the first time since blasting off in January. He rode home in a cushioned reclining seat on the shuttle's lower deck.
NASA doctors expected the 42-year-old navy captain would regain his "earth legs" within a few days and would make a full recovery of the debilitating effects of space travel within four months.
Linenger's 132-day mission was marred by a serious fire, numerous mechanical breakdowns and a near collision with an unmanned supply ship.

Atlantis, which blasted off on May 15, spent five days docked with the Russian orbital outpost. It left behind British-born U.S. astronaut Michael Foale for a four-month tour of duty and nearly two tonnes of supplies and equipment.
